tests: a malformed network-timeout override is ignored rather than honoured

consumesExternalOutput.program: git ls-remote --symref <remote> HEAD, against a TCP listener that accepts and never speaks
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: The mutated file src/pool.ts spawns git, so SPAWN_GREP matches and rule (f) binds. The capture is what makes both members DANGEROUS rather than merely wrong, and it is cited for that reason: it records that git waits forever when nothing answers, so a fallback that does not fire (member 0, where Number("") is 0 and spawnSync reads a timeout of 0 as NO TIMEOUT) and a shipped bound of 0 (member 1, the same unbounded state reached without touching the validation at all) both restore exactly the wait the capture shows. The two members are structurally different: one attacks the VALIDATION, the other the VALUE it falls back to, and an implementation could defend either alone.
